audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require recurring acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 strategic acquisitions $1.5bn, equal to 18.3% of the $8.2187bn OE anchor; nine-month FY2026 purchases of businesses and investments $3.004bn
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring acquisition cash required to sustain forecast growth would be reinvestment deducted from OE; any acquired-intangible amortization added back without corresponding acquisition spending compounds the overstatement.
audit_findings.evidence: Our disciplined acquisition strategy, which is an engine to fuel organic growth, is focused on scaling our business in high-growth areas; adding skills and capabilities in new areas; and deepening our industry and functional expertise.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring acquisition strategy and substantial cash spending are demonstrated, while the maintenance portion required for 5% or 8% growth is not. Because FY2025 spending alone exceeds the narrow $10.13 per-share gap between price and base value, a materially recurring portion is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Separate organic and acquired growth by year, trace acquired-intangible amortization in OE, estimate only the acquisition spending necessary to sustain each scenario, and rerun all scenarios with that recurring amount deducted.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 cash generation may include deferred compensation payments rather than sustainable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 accrued-payroll working-capital inflow $904.322m, equal to 11.0% of anchor OE; nine-month FY2026 inflow $647.825m
audit_findings.mechanism: An increase in accrued compensation raises operating cash flow and OE temporarily; normalization would reduce the OE anchor or future OE when employees are paid.
audit_findings.evidence: The $2,343 million increase in operating cash flows was primarily due to higher net income and lower cash outflows for certain compensation payments compared to the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-flow benefit is filed, but the record does not demonstrate whether the $8.2187bn anchor retained it or normalized it. If fully included, the FY2025 amount would reduce base value by approximately $20.72 per share under the existing base valuation mechanics, enough to reverse the modest apparent discount to base value.
audit_findings.action: Trace every FY2025 OE working-capital adjustment through accrued payroll and benefits, identify payment timing, normalize nonrecurring deferrals, and rerun the valuation if any amount remains in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Material uncertain-tax claims may not be reserved against added cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed reasonably possible 12-month increase in unrecognized tax benefits $1.4bn; latest current and non-current income taxes payable total $1.728155bn
audit_findings.mechanism: Any tax claim not already represented in normalized OE or recorded liabilities reduces cash available to equity and should reduce the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe that it is reasonably possible that our unrecognized tax benefits could decrease by approximately $ 187,000 or increase by approximately $ 1,400,000 in the next 12 months as a result of settlements, lapses of statutes of limitations, tax audit activity and other agreements with taxing authorities.
audit_findings.explanation: No omission is demonstrated because uncertain tax benefits and income-tax payables are already recorded. The supplied record does not reconcile those balances to the $10.171567bn cash addition or establish whether the possible $1.4bn change represents an incremental equity claim. If wholly incremental, $1.4bn equals about $2.05 per share and 1.0% of base equity value; the actual overlap and cash timing remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile unrecognized tax benefits, accrued interest and penalties, offsetting benefits, settlements, and latest tax-payable balances; rerun the bridge only for a verified incremental claim not already captured in OE or liabilities.

audit_findings.title: The DOJ investigation creates an unbounded claim not demonstrably reflected in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; AFS represented 8% of FY2025 consolidated revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: Penalties, forfeitures, settlement payments or lost federal contracts would reduce OE, while an incremental accrued claim would reduce the equity bridge; debarment could also reduce forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We cannot at this time determine when or how this matter will be resolved or estimate the cost or range of costs in excess of the amounts already accrued that are reasonably likely to be incurred in connection with this matter.
audit_findings.explanation: No excess loss is demonstrated, and the latest supplied 10-Q still says the amount cannot be estimated. Nevertheless, the active civil and criminal investigation can affect a business representing 8% of revenue and permits sanctions extending beyond a one-time cash payment. That exposure is reasonably capable of changing the growth or valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent filings and case developments for accrual changes, settlement terms, contract losses or debarment risk; then stress the affected AFS OE and growth separately and deduct any verified incremental claim.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement obligations may require cash beyond pension expense retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 pension and postretirement funded-status deficits total $1.655070bn; latest retirement obligation $1.910231bn; estimated FY2026 pension funding and benefit payments $170.941m
audit_findings.mechanism: Required funding above pension expense reduces future OE; alternatively, a deficit not otherwise captured may require an equity-bridge deduction, but both treatments must not be applied to the same obligation.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate we will pay approximately $ 170,941 in fiscal 2026 related to contributions to our U.S. and non-U.S. defined benefit pension plans and benefit payments related to the unfunded frozen plan for former pre-incorporation partners.
audit_findings.explanation: The underfunding and scheduled cash requirement are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether OE already captures contributions through operating cash-flow adjustments. The $170.941m annual amount is 2.1% of anchor OE, while the latest recorded obligation equals about $2.79 per share; materiality depends on the recurring excess over expense and existing OE treatment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense, non-operating pension components, contributions, benefit payments and OE cash-flow adjustments; rerun using either normalized excess funding or an after-tax bridge deduction without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Other noncontrolling interests can make the OE numerator inconsistent with the share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 other-NCI income $146.727m, equal to 1.8% of anchor OE and approximately $3.36 per share under base valuation mechanics
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated earnings and cash-flow adjustments attributable to nonexchangeable NCI must be removed because the diluted share denominator does not include those claims.
audit_findings.evidence: The income effect does not take into account “Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests - other,” since those shares are not redeemable or exchangeable for Accenture plc Class A ordinary shares.
audit_findings.explanation: A numerator error is not demonstrated without the OE construction. If the entire filed FY2025 other-NCI income were improperly included, base value would fall from $203.25 to approximately $199.89 per share and the corresponding buy-below level to approximately $139.92. Price would remain below base value but well above buy-below, so the known-scale item does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that each year's net income, D&A, working capital, capex and acquisition adjustments use the parent-equity perimeter; correct the numerator if consolidated amounts were used.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2020 residual D&A $750.7m, equal to 42.3% of filed D&A and 15.6% of FY2020 OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual component proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to historical OE; it does not directly enter the FY2025 OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $750.7m (42.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The conservative exclusion is demonstrated, but eligibility for an additional add-back is not. Although the residual is sizable relative to FY2020 OE, the valuation anchors on FY2025 actual OE because the existing trend is higher, so the FY2020 residual has no direct effect on the $8.2187bn anchor or current scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Classify the FY2020 residual from filed depreciation and amortization schedules; rerun the historical trend and anchor only if specific components are proven eligible for addition.
